mechanism_narrative: A rising FEDFUNDS rate above 1.5% in the current month predicts higher discount rates, which reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the identified FEDFUNDS > 1.5% regime.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in PAYEMS (labor market activity) by more than 2% month-over-month coincides with stronger consumer confidence and corporate hiring, which elevates expected future earnings and drives positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during the PAYEMS expansion threshold.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both HOUST (industrial production) and RSAFS (retail sales) above their prior month's levels indicates robust aggregate demand, which is associated with higher corporate earnings expectations and positive S&P 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) when both proxies exceed prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in INDPRO (industrial production index) by 3% over three months signals supply-side weakness, which raises uncertainty and compresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05) during the identified INDPRO contraction.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE (unemployment rate) falls below 4% for two consecutive months, it reflects labor market tightness that reduces risk aversion and supports higher equity valuations, producing positive S&P 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during the UNRATE < 4% regime.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in GDPC1 (real personal consumption) by 5% in the prior quarter is interpreted as a warning of near-term economic weakness, which depresses earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the GDPC1 decline.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in CPIAUCSL (CPI) of 0.3% or more suggests the Federal Reserve may cut rates soon, lowering discount rates and boosting equity present value, which predicts positive S&P 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during the CPIAUCSL decline.

mechanism_narrative: When both INDPRO and HOUST fall sequentially by at least 2% in the same month, it indicates dual supply-side shocks that raise uncertainty and compress valuations, resulting in negative S&P 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the sequential drop in both proxies.
